analyst_view.overall: Strasbourg (14th, 10 points, five defeats in six) sacked Hugo Oliveira this week and Vítor Matos, from Swansea, takes charge for the first time at the Meinau. Matos calls attacking football with pressing non-negotiable, but he confirmed Giovanni Reyna (scorer in the last game) and Oso will miss this one, on top of striker Panichelli; only Panichelli is counted by the numbers, and goalkeeper Jørgensen, a doubt after international duty, is now expected to start. Brest (9th, 15 points) arrive in form after beating Lorient and Lyon without conceding, missing only Chardonnet and Le Guen (counted), with Ajorque leading the line against his old club. Azzedine Souifi referees; the numbers know only four of his top-flight games and blend them with an average record.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, a high figure driven by Strasbourg's open games. Matos wants to attack, but he loses Reyna and Oso on top of Panichelli (only Panichelli is counted), so Strasbourg's attack is thinner than the numbers think; I trim slightly to about 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners. Both teams are expected in a 4-2-3-1 or 4-3-3, and a pressing start under Matos is close to how Strasbourg already play, so I stay at 8.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards. Souifi has only four games in the numbers, which already blend his record with an average referee, and Matos' pressing could bring a few fouls but nothing points to a heated game, so I stay at 3.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots. A new coach demanding intensity at home could add a few, while Reyna's and Oso's absences take some away, so I stay at 24.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. Without Reyna, Oso and Panichelli, Strasbourg lose much of their finishing and creativity, more than the numbers count, so I trim slightly to about 8.6.
